correction.text: the Colony and Protectorate: Lagos, Southern Nigeria and Northern Nigeria amalgamated

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; Nigeria sits in the British Africa aggregate until its Federal Republic row of 1961). 'in 1914 that was combined with the Northern Nigeria Protectorate to form the Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria'; the page gives no area (its infobox is garbled), and the Northern Nigeria page gives 660,000 km2 for the north in 1912. Modern Nigeria resolves to about 0.98 M km2 in the gazetteer; the north (twenty states, 0.76 M km2) is 78% of it, against 660,000 km2 for the north on the protectorate page. The British Cameroons are not in this outline: they were a mandate and trust territory administered with Nigeria (vassal events below).

Frederick Lugard is the first governor-general.

ledger.note: 1914 (1 January): the Northern Province, the Colony and the Southern Provinces are unified. The Northern Nigeria page: its area 'was unified with the Southern Nigeria Protectorate and the Lagos Colony'; the colony page: 1906 'merged the small Lagos Colony and the Southern Nigeria Protectorate into a new Colony of Southern Nigeria'.

region.text: the British share of Kamerun, 89,526 km2, in two parts: Northern and Southern Cameroons

ledger.note: 1916 (20 July): Britain and France divide German Kamerun. The British Cameroons infobox: 'Kamerun partitioned: 20 July 1916'; 'British and French forces divided the German colony during World War I, with the British taking the smaller share'.

region.text: the British share of Kamerun, 89,526 km2, in two parts: Northern and Southern Cameroons

ledger.note: 1922: the British share becomes a League of Nations mandate. The infobox: 'Class B League of Nations mandate under British administration (1922-1946)'; the Nigeria page dates the mandate 1920.

region.text: the British share of Kamerun, 89,526 km2, in two parts: Northern and Southern Cameroons

ledger.note: 1922: the Cameroons are administered with Nigeria. 'British Cameroons was still under the administration of Nigeria'; the Northern Cameroons later 'became the Sardauna Province of Northern Nigeria'. The UN approved the trusteeship agreement for the territory on 6 December 1946.

region.text: the British share of Kamerun, 89,526 km2, in two parts: Northern and Southern Cameroons

ledger.note: 1960 (1 October): Nigeria becomes independent while the Cameroons stay a UN trust territory. The Northern area voted on 11 February 1961 for Nigeria (joined 1 June 1961) and the Southern area for Cameroon (1 October 1961).

region.text: the Colony and Protectorate: Lagos, Southern Nigeria and Northern Nigeria amalgamated

ledger.note: 1960 (1 October): Nigeria becomes independent. 'until 1 October 1960, when Nigeria achieved independence.' The Western and Eastern Regions had become self-governing in 1957 and the Northern Region two years later.

wars.name: Kamerun campaign

zones.text: the British share of Kamerun, 89,526 km2, in two parts: Northern and Southern Cameroons

wars.outcome: Allied victory: Kamerun partitioned between Britain and France on 20 July 1916, the British taking the smaller share.
wars.note: The campaign article was not opened; the French Africa dossier (af-08-b) carries the campaign's dates.

certainty.note: The frontiers with Dahomey, Niger, Chad and Kamerun were fixed by Anglo-French and Anglo-German agreements that no page opened gives; the Lake Chad and Bakassi sectors stayed disputed ('governed by Nigeria until 2008').

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for the colony. The Southern Nigeria Protectorate (1900-1914) and the Lagos Colony (1861-1906) have dossiers by af-04 (niger-coast-protectorate, lagos-colony); the north is northern-nigeria-protectorate (this batch). The British Cameroons need their own dossier (counterpart british-cameroons, 1916-1961: flagged by af-08-c, af-08-g, af-08-h); the gazetteer lacks the region 'British Cameroons' (the researcher's reading: Southern Cameroons are the Nord-Ouest and Sud-Ouest regions of Cameroon, Northern Cameroons parts of the Adamawa and Taraba states of Nigeria).
Not settled: the infobox of the colony page is missing (no area, no day of founding); the Nigeria page puts the Cameroons mandate in 1920 and the British Cameroons page in 1922; Bakassi and Lake Chad frontiers; the Second World War moved no border and is not covered; the 1954 Lyttleton Constitution and the 1957/1959 self-government are administrative.
